question: For the reaction N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>(g) → 2NO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 1/2 O<sub>2</sub>(g), the rate of disappearance of N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub> is written as -d[N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>]/dt = k<sub>1</sub>[N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>]. The rates of formation of NO<sub>2</sub> and O<sub>2</sub> are written as d[NO<sub>2</sub>]/dt = k<sub>2</sub>[N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>] and d[O<sub>2</sub>]/dt = k<sub>3</sub>[N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>]. What is the relationship between k<sub>1</sub>, k<sub>2</sub>, and k<sub>3</sub>?
explanation: The rate of reaction is r = -d[N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>]/dt = 1/2 · d[NO<sub>2</sub>]/dt = 2 · d[O<sub>2</sub>]/dt. Substituting the rate expressions: k<sub>1</sub>[N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>] = 1/2 · k<sub>2</sub>[N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>] = 2 · k<sub>3</sub>[N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>]. Thus, k<sub>1</sub> = k<sub>2</sub>/2 = 2k<sub>3</sub>.

question: Which of the following represents the correct cell notation for the reaction: Mg(s) + 2Ag<sup>+</sup>(aq) → Mg<sup>2+</sup>(aq) + 2Ag(s)?
explanation: Mg is oxidized to Mg<sup>2+</sup> (anode, left side), and Ag<sup>+</sup> is reduced to Ag (cathode, right side). The phases are separated by single vertical lines, and the half-cells by a double vertical line.

question: In a thermochemical equation, C(graphite) + O<sub>2</sub>(g) → CO<sub>2</sub>(g), ΔH = -393.5 kJ. What does this representation imply about the stability of the product compared to the reactants?
options: Product is less stable than reactants
Product is more stable than reactants
Stability cannot be predicted from enthalpy
explanation: A negative ΔH (exothermic reaction) indicates that the product CO<sub>2</sub> lies at a lower potential energy level than the reactants, meaning it is thermodynamically more stable.

question: For the reaction 2A + B → 3C, if the rate of disappearance of A is 0.4 mol L<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>, what is the rate of the reaction?
explanation: The rate of reaction is r = -1/2 · d[A]/dt. Given -d[A]/dt = 0.4 mol L<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>, the rate of reaction is 0.4 / 2 = 0.2 mol L<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>.

question: How is the standard electrode potential of a half-cell represented when coupled with a Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE)?
options: By placing SHE always on the right
By placing SHE always on the left as the anode
By measuring the cell EMF under standard conditions with SHE as the reference
By ignoring the phase boundary of SHE
explanation: The standard electrode potential of any electrode is measured by coupling it with a SHE (whose potential is defined as 0.00 V) under standard conditions of concentration (1 M) and pressure (1 bar).
